71683.sol: Oxygen is a non-polar molecule, so it has very low solubility in polar solvents like water. 121302.subject: Botany
121302.text: What type of organisms are protozoans?
121302.sol: All protozoans are heterotrophs and live as predators or parasites. They are believed to be primitive relatives of animals. There are four major groups of protozoans.

121777.subject: Botany
121777.text: What do the spores germinate into in bryophytes?
121777.sol: They lack true roots, stems or leaves. They may possess root-like, leaf-like or stem-like structures. The main plant body of the bryophyte is haploid. It produces gametes, hence is called a gametophyte. The sex organs in bryophytes are multicellular. The male sex organ is called antheridium. They produce biflagellate antherozoids. 122456.subject: Botany
122456.text: Specific reproductive method Phylum A. Asexual reproduction by fragmentation 1. Sponges B. Metagenesis (alternation of generations) 2. Cnidarians C. Sexual reproduction with internal fertilization 3. Ctenophores D. Sexual reproduction with external fertilization 4. Platyhelminthes
122456.sol: Sponges reproduce asexually by fragmentation. Cnidarians exhibit metagenesis (alternation of generations). Platyhelminthes have sexual reproduction with internal fertilization. Ctenophores have sexual reproduction with external fertilization.

122558.text: Match List I with List II. List I List II (A) Pneumatic bones (I) Pristis (B) Air bladder (II) Crocodilus (C) Placoid scales (III) Corvus (D) Four-chambered heart in a poikilotherm (IV) Pterophyllum Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

122584.subject: Botany
122584.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding Myxine (Hagfish)?
options: Its cranium and vertebral column are cartilaginous.
Its body is devoid of scales.
Its circulatory system is of closed type.
It possesses paired fins for locomotion.
122584.sol: Myxine (Hagfish) belongs to the class Cyclostomata. Members of class Cyclostomata have an elongated body that is devoid of scales and paired fins. Thus, the statement that it possesses paired fins for locomotion is incorrect. Other characteristic features of cyclostomes include a cartilaginous cranium and vertebral column, and a closed type of circulatory system. Answer: It possesses paired fins for locomotion.

122732.subject: Botany
122732.text: What is the purpose of a flower in angiosperms?
122732.sol: The flower is the reproductive unit in the angiosperms. It is meant for sexual reproduction. A typical flower has four different kinds of whorls arranged successively on the swollen end of the stalk or pedicel, called thalamus or receptacle.These are calyx, corolla, androecium and gynoecium. Calyx and corolla are accessory organs, while androecium and gynoecium are reproductive organs.

122922.sol: Marginal placentation has a placenta forming a ridge, axile placentation has ovules attached to a central axis, parietal placentation involves ovules on the inner wall making the ovary appear two-chambered, and free central has ovules on a central axis with no septa.

124502.sol: In arithmetic growth, following mitotic cell division, only one daughter cell continues to divide while the other differentiates and matures. 125449.sol: Plants that are adapted to dry tropical regions have the C4 pathway mentioned earlier. C4 plants are special: They have a special type of leaf anatomy, they tolerate higher temperatures, they show a response to high light intensities, they lack a process called photorespiration and have greater productivity of biomass.

129369.subject: Zoology

129369.sol: The abducens nerve is the sixth paired cranial nerve. It has a purely somatic motor function-providing innervation to the lateral rectus muscle responsible for outward gaze. The six cranial nerves are the optic nerve (CN II), oculomotor nerve (CN III), trochlear nerve (CN IV), trigeminal nerve (CN V), abducens nerve (CN VI), and facial nerve (CN VII).
